title: The job that fired 200 times
blurb: A scheduler pause was followed by a catch-up burst.
prompt: After a ten-minute scheduler pause, a minutely job fired 200 catch-up executions in seconds and took down its downstream database. The model-generated draft retried each missed window and had no misfire policy. Review it, fix it, and prove misfires are policied, not stormed.
aiNote: The draft treats every missed window as owed and fires them all as fast as retries allow, so any scheduler pause converts into a burst against the target, and its last-run check-then-write lets two instances fire one window during a rolling deploy.
testIdea: Pause the scheduler for ten windows and assert at most one catch-up fire under fire-once; deploy two instances simultaneously and assert one fire per window; assert skipped windows appear in history with their policy.
followUps: Which jobs deserve catch-up versus skip?
How do you cap a catch-up burst?
What clock guarantees does the scheduler need across nodes?
